A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same cPLRNN research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The core material and appendices A–H can be matched reliably; v2 adds further material, including appendices I–J.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-training comparisons on Lorenz-63, LIF simulations and cortical-neuron recordings, alongside recovered equilibria and limit cycles (Figures 1–2, Tables 1–4).

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds heartbeat forecasting, stochastic Izhikevich-neuron experiments, and numerical robustness and scaling analyses (Section 4.5, appendices I–J).

M1.justification: The cPLRNN dynamics, interval-Newton switching solver, implicit differentiation, sparse teacher forcing and equilibrium/cycle detection procedures remain. Appendix D.2 and Algorithm 3 detail the matrix-perturbation and gradient-discard fallback already described in v1 Appendix A. The mathematical corrections do not establish a changed implementation or new method component.

E1.justification: V2 retains the original benchmarks and adds forecasting of irregular PhysioNet heart-rate series from ten subjects (Section 4.5, Appendix F.4), plus reconstruction of a stochastic Izhikevich neuron (Figure 6, Table 7). These substantially extend real-data coverage, task requirements and process-noise conditions.

E2.justification: V1 compares against discrete PLRNNs and Neural ODEs using Euler, RK4 and Tsit5. V2 additionally evaluates SINDy, Latent ODE and Neural CDE on the retained Lorenz, LIF and cortical-recording benchmarks (Tables 1, 3 and 4), substantially broadening the comparison methods.

E3.justification: V1 Table 4 explicitly evaluates cortical recordings in the original one-dimensional space; v2 Appendix G.1 specifies three-dimensional, noise-perturbed embeddings for neuron Dstsp evaluations. V2 also adds Lorenz prediction horizons, heartbeat forecasting with an 80/20 split, and sampling/perturbation sweeps. Its new Neural CDE comparison uses data-driven testing rather than autonomous rollout (Section 4.2).

E4.justification: V2 adds cycle-detection sensitivity to crossing-coordinate and flight-time initialization (Figure 7), expanded runtime scaling (Figure 8), ill-conditioning frequencies (Figure 9), a process-noise case study (Figure 6), and LIF sampling-density sensitivity (Table 7). These substantially extend v1's illustrative cycle examples and limited runtime comparison across P.

E5.justification: V2 adds 100-run initialization trials, 100-trajectory prediction summaries, a Wilcoxon comparison across heartbeat subjects and explicitly one-sided tests in Section 4.4. Table 3 describes 4/10 and 2/10 Euler runs as excluded rather than surviving. Prediction-time aggregation remains inconsistent: Table 1 specifies median/MAD, whereas Appendix G.3 specifies mean/standard deviation.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial benchmark, comparator, prediction-horizon and robustness results. Izhikevich results favor cPLRNN on Dstsp but standard PLRNN on DH (Table 7). Retained Lorenz P=10 cPLRNN Dstsp changes from 0.35±0.14 to 0.37±0.14, and Table 2 timings change. Revised neuron Dstsp values accompany changed evaluation conditions and do not establish comparable performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Equation 12 removes the erroneous constant bias term from the time derivative. Appendix D corrects the readout matrix to the appropriate N-by-M shape, and Equation 16 corrects the initial interval bound. The principal assumptions, cycle constraints and Appendix H theory remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and two introductory contributions retain the semi-analytical solver and tractable state-space analysis claims. The conclusion adds claimed advantages concerning continuous invariant-set geometry and universal approximation guarantees relative to discrete-time RNNs, modestly extending the central positioning.

C2.justification: V2 explains SINDy's function-library advantage and Latent ODE/Neural CDE rollout failures, connects LIF switching boundaries to resets, and interprets the cortical reconstruction as bistable. It also qualifies numerical and scaling limitations using new evidence and discusses initialization-dependent missed equilibria/cycles and the restriction to shallow architectures.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository pointer, Latent ODE/Neural CDE tuning grids, explicit eigenvalue and perturbation thresholds in Appendix D.2, heartbeat selection/preprocessing instructions, and CPU/core information for cycle detection. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the perturbation strategy itself was already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: The main related-work taxonomy and novelty framing remain. V2 adds cited positioning around SINDy, PhysioNet, causal Neural CDE interpolation, neuronal bistability, numerical continuation and continuous-time approximation guarantees, including Brunton et al. (2016), Morrill et al. (2021), and Sagodi and Park (2026).

P1.justification: Most existing exposition and the main section order are retained. V2 makes local language, terminology and cross-reference corrections, updates front matter, and adds Section 4.5 and supporting appendix subsections. The narrative changes are focused expansions rather than extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 3 and 6–9 and Tables 7–8, and restructures the Lorenz presentation: the earlier multi-P table becomes Table 9, while Table 1 adds comparators and prediction horizons. Figure 2 gains switching markers and a revised state-space projection. Existing appendix illustrations become Figures 4–5, with limited display corrections.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the method's practical claims through genuinely irregular real-data forecasting, stochastic-neuron reconstruction, and direct tests of scaling, conditioning and cycle-detection sensitivity. Correcting Equation 12 and adding implementation details and code-access information further improve correctness and reproducibility. Unequal rollout conditions for new baselines and inconsistent prediction-statistic descriptions limit some comparisons, but the added evidence addresses important gaps in v1.
